body.html:
Barkpark Cloud — Production Operator Console (epic wish)

A cloud where we feel in control. Most important: everything should work. Today the GUI can do almost nothing — we need to control webhooks and everything required to manage a studio, with a serious amount of features and toggles so it's actually production-ready. Very big epic.

The bar

Sanity's manage console (manage.sanity.io project view). Not its skin — its completeness: every meter live, every toggle wired, no dead panels, no curl-only capabilities.

The reference surface (Sanity manage, mapped to Barkpark Cloud)

A Sanity "project" ≈ a Barkpark instance. The console page for one instance carries:

Header: org label, instance name, plan, live status, project/org IDs with copy chips, primary "Open Studio →" action.

Tab IA: Overview / Members / Studios / API / Datasets / Access / Activity / Usage / Plan / Settings. Reconcile with the existing charter's D6 4-place nav — the instance DETAIL workspace is where this tab set lives (D6 already plans sub-tabs: Overview | Timeline | Env vars | Domains | Infrastructure | Danger). This epic EXPANDS that set.

Usage meters — each with plan quota + warning threshold state

• API requests / month, CDN requests / month
• Bandwidth / month, Asset storage
• Datasets n/n, Documents n/n (reference shows 45.5k/50k with warning state)
• Webhooks n/n, User seats n/n
Metering pipeline is in scope. Meters imply a per-instance metering subsystem (request counts, bandwidth, storage) — likely the biggest net-new subsystem. Meters without truth are lies.

Webhooks — EXPLICIT top user priority

"We need to control webhooks." Full parity from the GUI:

• Full CRUD: create / edit / delete, enable/disable toggle
• Dataset filter per hook, revalidation tags
• Delivery log: attempts, status codes, latencies, payload preview, REPLAY button
• Secret rotation
Architecture note. Webhooks live on the INSTANCE's content API (docs/contracts/webhook-realtime.md). The console reaches them through an instance-scoped control-plane proxy (precedent: the hetzner proxy, charter D3) or the on-box agent. The architect decides which; the browser never holds instance tokens.

The rest of the tab set

• Members & Access: avatar list, invite flow (email), roles, pending invites, remove, seat quota vs plan.
• Studios: list per instance, open/deploy, custom domain per studio, config.
• API: token CRUD (scoped), CORS origins management, API version surface.
• Datasets: create / copy / delete, visibility (public/private), per-dataset stats.
• Activity: audit feed with actor avatars, per-event detail, filters — builds on existing events/audit endpoints + charter D10 Timeline.
• Plan & Settings: plan display/upgrade path; real toggles — rename, transfer, danger zone (delete with D5 typed-name grammar), notification prefs.

CLI reciprocity: Sanity's "Blueprints stacks" copy-box ≈ charter D8 copy-as-CLI chips — every GUI capability shows its bp twin.

Non-negotiables

1. Everything works. A panel ships only with its live backend wired and tested. No decorative UI. (Charter __bpTestHook harness + __css_check gates apply to every slice.)
2. Control = toggles with truth. Every toggle reflects real server state, round-trips, and errors honestly.
3. Production-ready depth, not demo breadth. Quotas enforced + surfaced, warning states, empty/loading/error states per the charter's state grammar (roadmap 14).
4. Reconcile, don't discard. Charter decisions D1–D15 stand (SSE contract, token contract, proxy pattern, destructive-op grammar, one-app.js-slice-per-wave, attention-order spec). Waves 1–2 landed work is the foundation.
5. Security carries. Instance-scoped proxying, no tokens in the browser, audit events for every mutation.

Scale directive

"Very big epic — need very epic cycle." Plan MANY waves. Strategists think at full boldness (broader than the aesthetics epic it absorbs). The architect owns folding this into the charter as the superseding mission.
